newsitem.title: UK: EBRD head says crime, corruption still obstacles.
newsitem.headline: EBRD head says crime, corruption still obstacles.

text.p: EBRD president Jacques de Larosiere warned on Monday of the obstacles the bank still faces in eastern and central Europe, highlighting problems with legal frameworks, taxation systems, crime and corruption.

De Larosiere told the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development's annual meeting that such obstacles were encountered "all too often" by the bank and could harm or deter investment in the countries in which it operates.

While crime, corruption and "the arbitrary interference of some officials in private sector business activities" were far from being the rule, they remained a source of concern and had, in some cases "complicated or even compromised the bank's own operations", he told the meeting.

The uncertainty of, and gaps in, the legal framework of some countries were another obstacle to be overcome. "Investors need stable regulations, they must be able to enforce their contractual or shareholder rights," he said.
And "the enduring deficiencies of taxation systems" were most frequently cited by EBRD partners and potential investors as imposing excessive constraints on their activities.
De Larosiere said that the countries in which the EBRD operated were "still underperforming in terms of foreign investment and especially foreign direct investment".
